name: Jiuzi Holdings, Inc.

profile.description: Jiuzi Holdings, Inc. is a China-based micro-cap company originally engaged in franchising and operating new energy vehicle (NEV) retail stores under the 'Jiuzi' brand, selling battery-operated electric vehicles and plug-in electric vehicles in third- and fourth-tier Chinese cities. The company has recently pivoted toward cryptocurrency treasury management (adopting a policy to deploy up to $1 billion into select cryptocurrencies) and AI technology partnerships, while its core NEV retail business has effectively ceased generating meaningful revenue. Founded in 2019, incorporated in the Cayman Islands, and headquartered in Hangzhou, China. Market cap approximately $1.6M.

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): Jiuzi pivoted from NEV franchise retail to battery sales, generating $2.88M in FY2025 revenue — a 105% increase over FY2024's $1.40M [1]. However, trailing twelve-month revenue has since collapsed to just $97K, indicating the pivot did not produce sustainable results [2]. The company has announced additional pivots into cryptocurrency treasury management and AI imaging partnerships, but none have generated meaningful revenue [5][4]. AI Deployment (0/2): Jiuzi's subsidiary signed a strategic MoU with an AI technology company in May 2026 to explore next-generation intelligent imaging and data solutions [4], but no AI products are shipping and no AI-driven revenue or cost savings have been reported. Market Share (0/2): Jiuzi holds no meaningful market share in any category. The company is a negligible participant in China's NEV market, with 33 employees and $97K in trailing revenue against an industry dominated by BYD, NIO, and XPeng [1][2]. Product Pipeline (0/2): No specific next-generation products have been announced with launch dates or revenue visibility. The AI MoU and crypto partnerships are exploratory memoranda, not commercialized products [4][5]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No meaningful R&D spending is evident. With 33 employees and negligible revenue, the company lacks resources for significant research and development [1].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): No formal mission, vision, or purpose statement was found on the company's website or public materials. The closest articulation comes from CEO Zhang Hongye's press release statement about 'accelerating R&D and commercialization of innovative technologies while creating long-term shareholder value' [4], which is generic boilerplate interchangeable with any company. The company's original NEV retail business in underserved Chinese cities implied a purpose (clean transportation access), but no coherent mission has survived the rapid pivots from NEVs to batteries to crypto to AI. Community & Charitable Impact (0/2): No evidence of charitable giving, community programs, or philanthropic initiatives was found [1]. Employee Retention & Tenure (0/2): No employee retention data is available. The workforce of 33 employees operates under acute leadership instability — CEO Tao Li resigned in April 2026 and was replaced by Zhang Hongye in May 2026. The independent auditor (Audit Alliance LLP) was dismissed in June 2026 [3]. These signals suggest organizational turbulence rather than mission-driven retention. Insider Buying (0/2): No insider buying activity was identified. Instead, the company has pursued massive shareholder dilution through multiple private placements — including an $80M placement at $2/share and plans to expand financing to $1 billion — against a market capitalization of approximately $1.6M [5][6].

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: LIQUIDITY FLOOR TRIGGERED: Average daily volume of approximately 120,330 shares at $1.20 per share yields daily dollar volume of approximately $144,396, which is far below the $1,000,000 IOWN liquidity threshold [6]. Infrastructure score is therefore overridden to 0 regardless of underlying metrics. For reference, the mechanical score on available metrics would have been approximately 4/10 — D/E of 14% scores well (target <=70%), and FY2025 revenue growth of 105.89% YoY scores at maximum, but ROE of -140.61% and profit margin of -270.31% both score 0 [1][2]. Forward P/E and Forward PEG are unavailable (company is unprofitable with no analyst coverage). The company reported an accumulated deficit of $87.98M, operating loss of $10.19M in FY2025, and wrote off $8.73M in supplier advances [1]. Auditors raised substantial doubt about the company's ability to continue as a going concern [1].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9): Jiuzi's historical core business — franchising and operating physical NEV retail stores in Chinese third- and fourth-tier cities — involves in-person vehicle sales, physical inventory management, battery distribution logistics, and local franchise relationships that AI structurally cannot displace [1]. The company's newer crypto treasury strategy (Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB acquisitions and staking) is similarly not subject to AI substitution — cryptocurrency custody and yield generation are financial infrastructure operations [5]. No analysts cover JZXN for AI disruption risk given its micro-cap status, but the physical-world and financial-asset nature of both business lines provides inherent protection from AI displacement. The score is capped at 6 rather than 7+ because the company lacks any meaningful defensive moats (no proprietary data, no regulatory barriers, no switching costs) — the protection derives purely from the physical nature of operations rather than structural competitive advantages. AI Opportunity (0/1): Jiuzi signed an MoU with an AI technology company in May 2026 to explore imaging and data solutions [4], but no AI products have shipped and no AI-related revenue has been generated. The partnership remains exploratory with no quantifiable commercial output.

infinite_game.summary: Jiuzi Holdings is a textbook finite player. The company has no articulated Just Cause — its identity has shifted from NEV franchise retailer to battery seller to crypto treasury to AI partnerships within two years, chasing whatever sector is generating market excitement rather than pursuing an enduring purpose. Leadership instability (CEO replaced April 2026, auditor dismissed June 2026), going concern warnings, and a strategy built around private placement dilution rather than operational execution all signal a company playing to survive this quarter, not to keep playing indefinitely.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (0/3): No Just Cause is evident. The company exists to generate shareholder value through whatever business model is currently fashionable — NEV franchise retail, battery sales, crypto treasury, AI imaging — with no unifying vision of a better future that connects these pivots [1][4][5]. CEO Zhang Hongye's stated goal of 'creating long-term shareholder value' is the definition of a finite objective. The company's strategic direction changes every few months, driven by market trends and private placement fundraising rather than an enduring purpose. Sinek would identify this as a company with no cause to advance — it is playing to survive, not to contribute to something larger than itself.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Low-trust environment indicated by multiple red flags. CEO Tao Li resigned in April 2026 after leading the company's pivot to crypto, replaced by Zhang Hongye in May 2026 — representing fundamental leadership instability at the top [3]. The independent auditor (Audit Alliance LLP) was dismissed in June 2026, a serious governance concern that suggests friction between management and independent oversight [3]. The company has only 33 employees [2], yet has experienced COO appointments (Dr. Doug Buerger for crypto strategy), board reshuffles, and rapid strategic redirections that would create organizational whiplash even in a larger company. No evidence of employee empowerment, psychological safety, or cultural practices that create trust.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No evidence of an infinite competitive mindset. Management's public communications focus on 'strategic investments,' 'partnerships,' and fundraising milestones rather than learning from competitors or improving core capabilities [4][5]. In the NEV space, the company showed no awareness of what BYD, NIO, or other dominant players do better. In crypto, the strategy appears to be accumulation (1,000 BTC target) rather than competitive learning. The company's competitive language is absent rather than finite — it does not engage with rivals at all, operating in its own narrative of 'strategic transformation' disconnected from competitive reality.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The company has demonstrated willingness to dramatically change its business model — pivoting from NEV franchise retail to battery sales, then to cryptocurrency treasury management and AI technology partnerships within a two-year span [1][5][4]. These are not incremental changes; they represent fundamental shifts in what the company does and how it generates revenue. However, Sinek would not award the full 2 points because these pivots appear driven by financial desperation (collapsing revenue, going concern warnings, $88M accumulated deficit) rather than by a Just Cause [1]. True existential flexibility in Sinek's framework means abandoning what's working in service of purpose — Jiuzi is abandoning what's failing in search of survival. The flexibility is reactive, not visionary.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): No evidence of courageous long-term decisions. The company's strategic moves — crypto treasury adoption, AI MoUs, massive private placements — appear designed to generate market excitement and raise capital rather than build lasting capability [5]. The $1 billion private placement expansion from an initial $12M target suggests aggressive financial engineering rather than principled investment in future capability. CEO transitions (Tao Li to Zhang Hongye) and auditor dismissals suggest leadership is managing near-term crises, not making costly long-term bets. No examples were found of management sacrificing short-term results for enduring capability.

investment_thesis: Jiuzi Holdings generated $2.88M in FY2025 revenue from battery sales, a 105% increase over FY2024, demonstrating some execution capability in its NEV battery segment [1]. The company has secured strategic partnerships including a $30M investment from Xinhui Solar for Southeast Asia expansion (with plans to deliver 100+ electric heavy-duty trucks to Vietnam), an $80M private placement, and an MoU with an AI technology company for imaging and data solutions [4][5][7]. The appointment of CEO Zhang Hongye in May 2026, with background in automotive electronics and intelligent cockpit systems, could provide more focused technical leadership [3]. The company's extremely low debt (D/E of 14%) and net cash position ($334K cash against $10.6K debt) provide balance sheet flexibility for transformation efforts, and the Inspire Insight faith alignment score of 48 (ALIGNED) reflects positively on the company's ESG profile in its NEV-related operations.
thesis_continued: Jiuzi Holdings is a deeply distressed micro-cap with a market capitalization of approximately $1.6M, trailing twelve-month revenue of just $97K (down from $2.88M in FY2025), and an accumulated deficit of $88M [1][2]. Auditors have raised substantial doubt about the company's ability to continue as a going concern. The company wrote off $8.73M in supplier advances who failed to deliver vehicles, highlighting severe counterparty and credit risk [1]. The strategic direction is chaotic — pivoting from NEV retail to battery sales to crypto treasury to AI imaging within two years, with no pivot generating sustainable revenue. Leadership instability is acute: CEO Tao Li resigned in April 2026 and was replaced by Zhang Hongye, and the independent auditor was dismissed in June 2026 [3]. The stock is extremely illiquid (average daily volume ~120K shares at ~$1.20, yielding ~$144K daily dollar volume — far below the IOWN $1M liquidity threshold) and has declined approximately 98% in the last 52 weeks [6]. Multiple private placements totaling hundreds of millions of dollars against a $1.6M market cap represent extreme dilution risk for existing shareholders [5].
key_catalysts: Execution on the AI imaging and data solutions MoU with potential commercialization in smart retail and autonomous driving applications, providing a new revenue stream beyond the collapsed NEV business
Southeast Asia expansion through the Xinhui Solar partnership and delivery of 100+ electric heavy-duty trucks to Vietnam, opening a new geographic market with growing EV demand
Crypto treasury strategy generating yield through SOLV Foundation Bitcoin staking vault and potential appreciation of Bitcoin, Ethereum, and BNB holdings if digital asset markets remain favorable
key_risks: Going concern doubt from auditors with accumulated deficit of $88M, TTM revenue of only $97K, and operating losses exceeding $10M annually — the company may not survive as a going concern without continuous capital raises

Chaotic strategic pivots from NEV retail to batteries to crypto to AI with no consistent direction, CEO replacement in April 2026, and auditor dismissal in June 2026 fundamentally undermine operational credibility and governance

Extreme illiquidity (average daily dollar volume ~$144K, far below IOWN's $1M threshold) and massive shareholder dilution through private placements ($80M+ in share issuances against a $1.6M market cap) create severe capital destruction risk for existing shareholders
